topic: Electron Dot Diagrams and Periodic Table Blocks
key_concepts: Valence electrons are the outermost electrons of an atom
Electron configuration determines the number of valence electrons
Electron dot diagrams use the element symbol and dots to show valence electrons
Dots are placed singly around the symbol before pairing because electrons repel each other
The periodic table is divided into s, p, d, and f blocks based on orbitals
Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons
Elements in the same group have similar properties
Lithium has one valence electron, oxygen has six, and iron has two in its ground state
Shells are circular paths around the nucleus in Bohr's model
Transition metals have varied numbers of valence electrons due to energy level changes
